summary: Brompton Cemetery is a garden cemetery in West Brompton, in London's Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea. It opened in 1840 and is one of London's "Magnificent Seven" cemeteries, built by private companies because inner-city burial grounds could no longer cope. Since 1852 it has been the only London cemetery owned by the Crown, and The Royal Parks manages it. About 35,000 monuments mark more than 205,000 graves. Architect Benjamin Bauda designed it to feel like an open-air cathedral, with a domed chapel and colonnades above catacombs. The catacombs sold poorly, and the company's shareholders were glad to sell once an 1850 Act let the government buy such cemeteries. The site is listed Grade I. From 1854 to 1939 it was the London District's military cemetery. It still takes burials and is known as a haven for nature. A restoration funded by a National Lottery grant was finished in 2018.
